input: South West Africa became known as Namibia by the UN when the General Assembly changed the territory's name by Resolution 2372 (XXII) of 12 June 1968. In 1978 the UN Security Council passed UN Resolution 435 which planned a transition toward independence for Namibia. Attempts to persuade South Africa to agree to the plan's implementation were not successful until 1988 when the transition to independence finally started under a diplomatic agreement between South Africa, Angola and Cuba, with the USSR and the USA as observers, under which South Africa agreed to withdraw and demobilise its forces in Namibia. As a result, Cuba agreed to pull back its troops in southern Angola sent to support the MPLA in its war for control of Angola with UNITA.
rewrite: South West Africa was renamed Namibia by the UN General Assembly through Resolution 2372 (XXII) on 12 June 1968. In 1978, the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 435, outlining a plan for Namibian independence. Efforts to secure South Africa's compliance with this plan were unsuccessful until 1988. At that time, a diplomatic agreement involving South Africa, Angola, and Cuba—with the USSR and the USA as observers—initiated the transition. Under this accord, South Africa agreed to withdraw and demobilize its forces from Namibia. Consequently, Cuba agreed to withdraw its troops from southern Angola, where they had been supporting the MPLA in its war against UNITA for control of Angola.

input: Von Neumann worked on lattice theory between 1937 and 1939. Von Neumann provided an abstract exploration of dimension in completed complemented modular topological lattices: "Dimension is determined, up to a positive linear transformation, by the following two properties. It is conserved by perspective mappings ("perspectivities") and ordered by inclusion. The deepest part of the proof concerns the equivalence of perspectivity with "projectivity by decomposition"—of which a corollary is the transitivity of perspectivity." Garrett Birkhoff writes: "John von Neumann's brilliant mind blazed over lattice theory like a meteor".
rewrite: Between 1937 and 1939, John von Neumann contributed to lattice theory with an abstract exploration of dimension in completed complemented modular topological lattices. He stated that dimension is determined, up to a positive linear transformation, by two properties: it is conserved by perspectivities and ordered by inclusion. A key part of the proof establishes the equivalence of perspectivity with "projectivity by decomposition," a corollary of which is the transitivity of perspectivity. Garrett Birkhoff remarked that von Neumann's brilliant mind "blazed over lattice theory like a meteor."

input: From early in its development, ASCII was intended to be just one of several national variants of an international character code standard, ultimately published as ISO/IEC 646 (1972), which would share most characters in common but assign other locally useful characters to several code points reserved for "national use." However, the four years that elapsed between the publication of ASCII-1963 and ISO's first acceptance of an international recommendation during 1967 caused ASCII's choices for the national use characters to seem to be de facto standards for the world, causing confusion and incompatibility once other countries did begin to make their own assignments to these code points.
rewrite: From its early development, ASCII was designed as one of several national variants within an international character code standard, later published as ISO/IEC 646 (1972). This standard shared most characters but reserved certain code points for "national use," allowing local adaptations. Yet the four-year gap between ASCII's publication in 1963 and ISO's initial international recommendation in 1967 led ASCII's selections for these national-use characters to become de facto global standards. This resulted in confusion and incompatibility when other countries eventually assigned their own characters to the same code points.

input: A striking technical innovation of the Komnenian period was the production of very precious, miniature mosaic icons. In these icons the small tesserae (with sides of 1 mm or less) were set on wax or resin on a wooden panel. These products of extraordinary craftmanship were intended for private devotion. The Louvre Transfiguration is a very fine example from the late 12th century. The miniature mosaic of Christ in the Museo Nazionale at Florence illustrates the more gentle, humanistic conception of Christ which appeared in the 12th century.
rewrite: A striking technical innovation of the Komnenian period was the creation of highly precious, miniature mosaic icons. These icons featured exceptionally small tesserae, with sides measuring 1 mm or less, set into wax or resin on a wooden panel. Products of extraordinary craftsmanship, they were intended for private devotion. A very fine example from the late 12th century is the Louvre Transfiguration. Meanwhile, the miniature mosaic of Christ in the Museo Nazionale at Florence illustrates the more gentle, humanistic conception of Christ that emerged in the 12th century.

input: Modern Orthodoxy, as a stream of Orthodox Judaism represented by institutions such as the U.S. National Council for Young Israel, is pro-Zionist and thus places a high national, as well as religious, significance on the State of Israel, and its affiliates are, typically, Zionist in orientation. It also practices involvement with non-Orthodox Jews that extends beyond "outreach (Kiruv)" to continued institutional relations and cooperation; see further under Torah Umadda. Other "core beliefs" are a recognition of the value and importance of secular studies, a commitment to equality of education for both men and women, and a full acceptance of the importance of being able to financially support oneself and one's family.
rewrite: Modern Orthodoxy, a stream of Orthodox Judaism represented by institutions like the U.S. National Council for Young Israel, is pro-Zionist. It therefore attributes high national and religious significance to the State of Israel, and its affiliates are typically Zionist in orientation. This movement also engages with non-Orthodox Jews, extending beyond "outreach (Kiruv)" to maintain ongoing institutional relations and cooperation, as further detailed under Torah Umadda. Other core beliefs include recognizing the value of secular studies, committing to equal education for men and women, and fully accepting the importance of achieving financial self-sufficiency for oneself and one's family.

input: Strasbourg is situated on the eastern border of France with Germany. This border is formed by the River Rhine, which also forms the eastern border of the modern city, facing across the river to the German town Kehl. The historic core of Strasbourg however lies on the Grande Île in the River Ill, which here flows parallel to, and roughly 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) from, the Rhine. The natural courses of the two rivers eventually join some distance downstream of Strasbourg, although several artificial waterways now connect them within the city.
rewrite: Strasbourg lies on France's eastern border with Germany, a boundary formed by the River Rhine. The Rhine also serves as the modern city's eastern border, facing the German town of Kehl across the river. The historic core of Strasbourg, however, is located on the Grande Île in the River Ill, which flows parallel to the Rhine roughly 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) away. The natural courses of the two rivers join downstream from the city, though several artificial waterways now connect them within Strasbourg.

input: As Universal's main product had always been low-budget film, it was one of the last major studios to have a contract with Technicolor. The studio did not make use of the three-strip Technicolor process until Arabian Nights (1942), starring Jon Hall and Maria Montez. The following year, Technicolor was also used in Universal's remake of their 1925 horror melodrama, Phantom of the Opera with Claude Rains and Nelson Eddy. With the success of their first two pictures, a regular schedule of high-budget, Technicolor films followed.
rewrite: Universal had long focused on low-budget films, making it one of the last major studios to sign a contract with Technicolor. The studio first employed the three-strip Technicolor process for Arabian Nights (1942), starring Jon Hall and Maria Montez. The next year, Technicolor was used in Universal's remake of its 1925 horror melodrama, Phantom of the Opera, featuring Claude Rains and Nelson Eddy. Encouraged by the success of these two pictures, the studio then established a regular schedule of high-budget Technicolor films.

input: Digimon started out as digital pets called "Digital Monsters", similar in style and concept to the Tamagotchi. It was planned by WiZ and released by Bandai on June 26, 1997. The toy began as the simple concept of a Tamagotchi mainly for boys. The V-Pet is similar to its predecessors, with the exceptions of being more difficult and being able to fight other Digimon v-pets. Every owner would start with a Baby Digimon, train it, evolve it, take care of it, and then have battles with other Digimon owners to see who was stronger. The Digimon pet had several evolution capabilities and abilities too, so many owners had different Digimon. In December, the second generation of Digital Monster was released, followed by a third edition in 1998.
rewrite: Originally launched as "Digital Monsters," Digimon began as digital pets akin to Tamagotchi. Developed by WiZ and released by Bandai on June 26, 1997, the toy was conceived as a Tamagotchi-style device primarily aimed at boys. While similar to its predecessors, the V-Pet was notably more challenging and introduced the ability to battle other Digimon devices. Each owner would raise a Baby Digimon, caring for it, training it, and evolving it, before engaging in battles with other owners to determine strength. The pets possessed various evolution paths and abilities, leading to a diversity of Digimon among owners. A second generation was released in December, with a third edition following in 1998.

input: The element was probably named by the alchemist Paracelsus after the German word Zinke (prong, tooth). German chemist Andreas Sigismund Marggraf is credited with discovering pure metallic zinc in 1746. Work by Luigi Galvani and Alessandro Volta uncovered the electrochemical properties of zinc by 1800. Corrosion-resistant zinc plating of iron (hot-dip galvanizing) is the major application for zinc. Other applications are in batteries, small non-structural castings, and alloys, such as brass. A variety of zinc compounds are commonly used, such as zinc carbonate and zinc gluconate (as dietary supplements), zinc chloride (in deodorants), zinc pyrithione (anti-dandruff shampoos), zinc sulfide (in luminescent paints), and zinc methyl or zinc diethyl in the organic laboratory.
rewrite: The element was likely named by the alchemist Paracelsus, deriving from the German word "Zinke," meaning prong or tooth. Pure metallic zinc is credited to the German chemist Andreas Sigismund Marggraf, who discovered it in 1746. By 1800, Luigi Galvani and Alessandro Volta had revealed zinc's electrochemical properties. Its major application is in corrosion-resistant zinc plating for iron, known as hot-dip galvanizing. Other uses include batteries, small non-structural castings, and alloys like brass. Commonly used zinc compounds range from dietary supplements (zinc carbonate, zinc gluconate) to ingredients in deodorants (zinc chloride), anti-dandruff shampoos (zinc pyrithione), luminescent paints (zinc sulfide), and organic laboratory reagents (zinc methyl, zinc diethyl).

input: During the 1920s and 1930s, British civil servants and politicians, looking back at the performance of the state during World War I, concluded that there was a need for greater co-ordination between the three Services that made up the armed forces of the United Kingdom—the British Army, the Royal Navy, and the Royal Air Force. The formation of a united ministry of defence was rejected by David Lloyd George's coalition government in 1921; but the Chiefs of Staff Committee was formed in 1923, for the purposes of inter-Service co-ordination. As rearmament became a concern during the 1930s, Stanley Baldwin created the position of Minister for Coordination of Defence. Lord Chatfield held the post until the fall of Neville Chamberlain's government in 1940; his success was limited by his lack of control over the existing Service departments and his limited political influence.
rewrite: In the 1920s and 1930s, British officials and politicians reflected on the state’s performance in World War I and concluded that better coordination was needed among the three Services of the United Kingdom’s armed forces: the British Army, the Royal Navy, and the Royal Air Force. Although David Lloyd George’s coalition government rejected a unified ministry of defence in 1921, the Chiefs of Staff Committee was established in 1923 to facilitate inter-Service coordination. As rearmament grew urgent in the 1930s, Stanley Baldwin created the role of Minister for Coordination of Defence. Lord Chatfield occupied this post until Neville Chamberlain’s government fell in 1940, but his effectiveness was constrained by his limited authority over the separate Service departments and his modest political influence.

input: Under contract from the U.S. Military, Matrox produced a combination computer/LaserDisc player for instructional purposes. The computer was a 286, the LaserDisc player only capable of reading the analog audio tracks. Together they weighed 43 lb (20 kg) and sturdy handles were provided in case two people were required to lift the unit. The computer controlled the player via a 25-pin serial port at the back of the player and a ribbon cable connected to a proprietary port on the motherboard. Many of these were sold as surplus by the military during the 1990s, often without the controller software. Nevertheless, it is possible to control the unit by removing the ribbon cable and connecting a serial cable directly from the computer's serial port to the port on the LaserDisc player.
rewrite: Under contract with the U.S. Military, Matrox developed a combined computer and LaserDisc player for training. The computer featured a 286 processor, while the LaserDisc player could only read analog audio tracks. The entire unit weighed 43 lb (20 kg), and sturdy handles were included in case two people needed to lift it. The computer controlled the player through a 25-pin serial port on the back of the player, connected via a ribbon cable to a proprietary port on the motherboard. Many of these units were sold as military surplus in the 1990s, frequently without the original controller software. However, control is still possible by removing the ribbon cable and connecting a serial cable directly from the computer's serial port to the port on the LaserDisc player.

input: In the United Kingdom, a bill is presented for royal assent after it has passed all the required stages in both the House of Commons and the House of Lords. Under the Parliament Acts 1911 and 1949, the House of Commons may, under certain circumstances, direct that a bill be presented for assent despite lack of passage by the House of Lords. Officially, assent is granted by the sovereign or by Lords Commissioners authorised to act by letters patent. It may be granted in parliament or outside parliament; in the latter case, each house must be separately notified before the bill takes effect.
rewrite: In the United Kingdom, a bill is presented for royal assent after completing all necessary stages in both the House of Commons and the House of Lords. However, under the Parliament Acts 1911 and 1949, the House of Commons may, in certain circumstances, direct that a bill be presented for assent even without passage by the House of Lords. Officially, assent is granted by the sovereign or by Lords Commissioners authorized to act via letters patent. This assent may be granted either in parliament or outside parliament; if outside, each house must be separately notified before the bill takes effect.

input: In the late eighteenth- and early nineteenth-century Germany, three pioneer physical educators – Johann Friedrich GutsMuths (1759–1839) and Friedrich Ludwig Jahn (1778–1852) – created exercises for boys and young men on apparatus they had designed that ultimately led to what is considered modern gymnastics. Don Francisco Amorós y Ondeano, was born on February 19, 1770 in Valence and died on August 8, 1848 in Paris. He was a Spanish colonel, and the first person to introduce educative gymnastic in France. Jahn promoted the use of parallel bars, rings and high bar in international competition.
rewrite: In late eighteenth- and early nineteenth-century Germany, two pioneer physical educators—Johann Friedrich GutsMuths (1759–1839) and Friedrich Ludwig Jahn (1778–1852)—designed apparatus exercises for boys and young men. These innovations ultimately led to modern gymnastics. Jahn specifically promoted the parallel bars, rings, and high bar for international competition. Separately, Don Francisco Amorós y Ondeano (born February 19, 1770, in Valence; died August 8, 1848, in Paris) was a Spanish colonel who first introduced educative gymnastics to France.

input: As the President, Tito had access to extensive (state-owned) property associated with the office, and maintained a lavish lifestyle. In Belgrade he resided in the official residence, the Beli dvor, and maintained a separate private home. The Brijuni islands were the site of the State Summer Residence from 1949 on. The pavilion was designed by Jože Plečnik, and included a zoo. Close to 100 foreign heads of state were to visit Tito at the island residence, along with film stars such as Elizabeth Taylor, Richard Burton, Sophia Loren, Carlo Ponti, and Gina Lollobrigida.
rewrite: As President, Tito enjoyed the use of extensive state-owned property, which supported his lavish lifestyle. His official residence in Belgrade was the Beli dvor, though he also kept a private home. From 1949 onward, the Brijuni islands hosted the State Summer Residence. Designed by Jože Plečnik, its pavilion complex included a zoo. Nearly 100 foreign heads of state visited Tito there, as did film stars like Elizabeth Taylor, Richard Burton, Sophia Loren, Carlo Ponti, and Gina Lollobrigida.

input: The tradition holds that Virgil was born in the village of Andes, near Mantua in Cisalpine Gaul. Analysis of his name has led to beliefs that he descended from earlier Roman colonists. Modern speculation ultimately is not supported by narrative evidence either from his own writings or his later biographers. Macrobius says that Virgil's father was of a humble background; however, scholars generally believe that Virgil was from an equestrian landowning family which could afford to give him an education. He attended schools in Cremona, Mediolanum, Rome and Naples. After considering briefly a career in rhetoric and law, the young Virgil turned his talents to poetry.
rewrite: According to tradition, Virgil was born in Andes, a village near Mantua in Cisalpine Gaul. Analysis of his name suggests descent from earlier Roman colonists, though such modern speculation lacks support from his own writings or later biographers. Macrobius claims Virgil's father was of humble origins, yet scholars generally hold that he came from an equestrian landowning family capable of providing an education. Virgil attended schools in Cremona, Mediolanum, Rome, and Naples. Briefly considering a career in rhetoric and law, he ultimately devoted his talents to poetry.

input: Longstanding political tensions from the 27 year rule of William Tubman resulted in a military coup in 1980 that overthrew the leadership soon after his death, marking the beginning of political instability. Five years of military rule by the People's Redemption Council and five years of civilian rule by the National Democratic Party of Liberia were followed by the First and Second Liberian Civil Wars. These resulted in the deaths and displacement of more than half a million people and devastated Liberia's economy. A peace agreement in 2003 led to democratic elections in 2005. Recovery proceeds but about 85% of the population live below the international poverty line.
rewrite: Longstanding political tensions from William Tubman's 27-year rule culminated in a military coup in 1980, which overthrew the leadership soon after his death and initiated a period of instability. This was followed by five years of military rule under the People's Redemption Council and five years of civilian rule by the National Democratic Party of Liberia, preceding the First and Second Liberian Civil Wars. The conflicts caused over half a million deaths and displacements, devastating Liberia's economy. A 2003 peace agreement led to democratic elections in 2005. Recovery continues, yet approximately 85% of the population lives below the international poverty line.

input: The production for sulfidic zinc ores produces large amounts of sulfur dioxide and cadmium vapor. Smelter slag and other residues of process also contain significant amounts of heavy metals. About 1.1 million tonnes of metallic zinc and 130 thousand tonnes of lead were mined and smelted in the Belgian towns of La Calamine and Plombières between 1806 and 1882. The dumps of the past mining operations leach significant amounts of zinc and cadmium, and, as a result, the sediments of the Geul River contain significant amounts of heavy metals. About two thousand years ago emissions of zinc from mining and smelting totaled 10 thousand tonnes a year. After increasing 10-fold from 1850, zinc emissions peaked at 3.4 million tonnes per year in the 1980s and declined to 2.7 million tonnes in the 1990s, although a 2005 study of the Arctic troposphere found that the concentrations there did not reflect the decline. Anthropogenic and natural emissions occur at a ratio of 20 to 1.
rewrite: The processing of sulfidic zinc ores generates substantial sulfur dioxide and cadmium vapor. Smelter slag and other industrial residues also hold significant quantities of heavy metals. From 1806 to 1882, approximately 1.1 million tonnes of metallic zinc and 130 thousand tonnes of lead were mined and smelted in the Belgian towns of La Calamine and Plombières. Waste from these historical mining activities leaches considerable zinc and cadmium, leading to high levels of heavy metals in the sediments of the Geul River. Around two thousand years ago, annual zinc emissions from mining and smelting reached 10 thousand tonnes. After rising tenfold from 1850, these emissions peaked at 3.4 million tonnes per year in the 1980s before falling to 2.7 million tonnes in the 1990s; however, a 2005 study of the Arctic troposphere found its concentrations did not mirror this decrease. Anthropogenic and natural emissions currently occur at a ratio of 20 to 1.

input: The first written account of a game played was on October 15, 1862, on the Montreal Cricket Grounds. It was between the First Battalion Grenadier Guards and the Second Battalion Scots Fusilier Guards resulting in a win by the Grenadier Guards 3 goals, 2 rouges to nothing.[citation needed] In 1864, at Trinity College, Toronto, F. Barlow Cumberland, Frederick A. Bethune, and Christopher Gwynn, one of the founders of Milton, Massachusetts, devised rules based on rugby football. The game gradually gained a following, with the Hamilton Football Club formed on November 3, 1869, (the oldest football club in Canada). Montreal formed a team April 8, 1872, Toronto was formed on October 4, 1873, and the Ottawa FBC on September 20, 1876.
rewrite: The first recorded game was played on October 15, 1862, at the Montreal Cricket Grounds. It featured the First Battalion Grenadier Guards against the Second Battalion Scots Fusilier Guards, with the Grenadier Guards winning by a score of 3 goals and 2 rouges to nothing. In 1864, at Trinity College in Toronto, F. Barlow Cumberland, Frederick A. Bethune, and Christopher Gwynn—one of the founders of Milton, Massachusetts—established rules based on rugby football. The sport slowly grew in popularity. The Hamilton Football Club, the oldest football club in Canada, was formed on November 3, 1869. A Montreal team followed on April 8, 1872, a Toronto club was established on October 4, 1873, and the Ottawa FBC was created on September 20, 1876.

input: In 1982, Regis McKenna was brought in to shape the marketing and launch of the Macintosh. Later the Regis McKenna team grew to include Jane Anderson, Katie Cadigan and Andy Cunningham, who eventually led the Apple account for the agency. Cunningham and Anderson were the primary authors of the Macintosh launch plan. The launch of the Macintosh pioneered many different tactics that are used today in launching technology products, including the "multiple exclusive," event marketing (credited to John Sculley, who brought the concept over from Pepsi), creating a mystique around a product and giving an inside look into a product's creation.
rewrite: In 1982, Regis McKenna was enlisted to oversee the marketing and launch of the Macintosh. His team later expanded to include Jane Anderson, Katie Cadigan, and Andy Cunningham, with Cunningham eventually leading the Apple account for the agency. Cunningham and Anderson served as the primary authors of the Macintosh launch plan. This launch pioneered numerous tactics still used in technology product introductions today. These included the "multiple exclusive," event marketing—a concept credited to John Sculley, who brought it from Pepsi—along with creating product mystique and offering an inside view into the product's creation.

input: As of 2012, renewable energy plays a major role in the energy mix of many countries globally. Renewables are becoming increasingly economic in both developing and developed countries. Prices for renewable energy technologies, primarily wind power and solar power, continued to drop, making renewables competitive with conventional energy sources. Without a level playing field, however, high market penetration of renewables is still dependent on a robust promotional policies. Fossil fuel subsidies, which are far higher than those for renewable energy, remain in place and quickly need to be phased out.
rewrite: As of 2012, renewable energy is a major part of the energy mix in many countries worldwide. It is becoming increasingly economical in both developing and developed nations. Prices for technologies like wind and solar power have continued to fall, making renewables competitive with conventional sources. However, without a level playing field, high market penetration still relies on strong promotional policies. Fossil fuel subsidies, which remain far higher than those for renewables, need to be phased out quickly.

input: The region, as part of Lorraine, was part of the Holy Roman Empire, and then was gradually annexed by France in the 17th century, and formalized as one of the provinces of France. The Calvinist manufacturing republic of Mulhouse, known as Stadtrepublik Mülhausen, became a part of Alsace after a vote by its citizens on 4 January 1798. Alsace is frequently mentioned with and as part of Lorraine and the former duchy of Lorraine, since it was a vital part of the duchy, and later because German possession as the imperial province (Alsace-Lorraine, 1871–1918) was contested in the 19th and 20th centuries; France and Germany exchanged control of parts of Lorraine (including Alsace) four times in 75 years.
rewrite: The region, historically part of Lorraine, belonged to the Holy Roman Empire before being gradually annexed by France in the 17th century and formalized as a French province. The Calvinist manufacturing republic of Mulhouse, or Stadtrepublik Mülhausen, joined Alsace following a vote by its citizens on 4 January 1798. Alsace is often mentioned alongside and as part of Lorraine, referencing the former duchy to which it was integral. This connection persisted because German possession as the imperial province of Alsace-Lorraine (1871–1918) was contested in the 19th and 20th centuries; control of parts of Lorraine, including Alsace, shifted between France and Germany four times in 75 years.

input: Armenians have had a presence in the Armenian Highland for over four thousand years, since the time when Hayk, the legendary patriarch and founder of the first Armenian nation, led them to victory over Bel of Babylon. Today, with a population of 3.5 million, they not only constitute an overwhelming majority in Armenia, but also in the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh. Armenians in the diaspora informally refer to them as Hayastantsis (Հայաստանցի), meaning those that are from Armenia (that is, those born and raised in Armenia). They, as well as the Armenians of Iran and Russia speak the Eastern dialect of the Armenian language. The country itself is secular as a result of Soviet domination, but most of its citizens identify themselves as Apostolic Armenian Christian.
rewrite: Armenians have lived in the Armenian Highland for more than four thousand years, dating back to the legendary patriarch Hayk, who led them to victory over Bel of Babylon and founded the first Armenian nation. Today, with a population of 3.5 million, they form an overwhelming majority not only in Armenia itself but also in the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh. Those from Armenia are informally called Hayastantsis (Հայաստանցի) in the diaspora, meaning people born and raised in Armenia. These Hayastantsis, along with Armenians in Iran and Russia, speak the Eastern dialect of the Armenian language. Although the country is secular due to Soviet rule, most citizens identify as Apostolic Armenian Christians.

input: According to a National Geographic article, the novel is so revered in Monroeville that people quote lines from it like Scripture; yet Harper Lee herself refused to attend any performances, because "she abhors anything that trades on the book's fame". To underscore this sentiment, Lee demanded that a book of recipes named Calpurnia's Cookbook not be published and sold out of the Monroe County Heritage Museum. David Lister in The Independent states that Lee's refusal to speak to reporters made them desire to interview her all the more, and her silence "makes Bob Dylan look like a media tart". Despite her discouragement, a rising number of tourists made to Monroeville a destination, hoping to see Lee's inspiration for the book, or Lee herself. Local residents call them "Mockingbird groupies", and although Lee was not reclusive, she refused publicity and interviews with an emphatic "Hell, no!"

input: The Hanoverian king George II of Great Britain was passionately devoted to his family’s continental holdings, but his commitments in Germany were counterbalanced by the demands of the British colonies overseas. If war against France for colonial expansion was to be resumed, then Hanover had to be secured against Franco-Prussian attack. France was very much interested in colonial expansion and was willing to exploit the vulnerability of Hanover in war against Great Britain, but it had no desire to divert forces to central Europe for Prussia's interest.
rewrite: King George II of Great Britain was deeply committed to his family's continental lands in Hanover. However, these German interests were balanced by the demands of Britain's overseas colonies. To resume a war with France for colonial expansion, Hanover needed protection from a Franco-Prussian attack. France, also eager for colonial gains, was willing to target Hanover's vulnerability in a conflict with Britain. Yet, it had no wish to divert its forces into central Europe merely for Prussia's benefit.

input: Meanwhile, with the advent and popularity of Internet-based distribution of files in lossily-compressed audio formats such as MP3, sales of CDs began to decline in the 2000s. For example, between 2000 - 2008, despite overall growth in music sales and one anomalous year of increase, major-label CD sales declined overall by 20%, although independent and DIY music sales may be tracking better according to figures released 30 March 2009, and CDs still continue to sell greatly. As of 2012, CDs and DVDs made up only 34 percent of music sales in the United States. In Japan, however, over 80 percent of music was bought on CDs and other physical formats as of 2015.
rewrite: Meanwhile, the rise of Internet-based file sharing and the popularity of lossily-compressed audio formats like MP3 led to a decline in CD sales during the 2000s. For instance, between 2000 and 2008, major-label CD sales fell by 20% overall, despite growth in total music sales and one year of increase. Figures released on 30 March 2009 suggested independent and DIY music sales may have fared better, and CDs still sold in significant quantities. By 2012, CDs and DVDs accounted for only 34 percent of music sales in the United States. In contrast, as of 2015, over 80 percent of music in Japan was purchased on CDs and other physical formats.

input: Following the Norman Conquest in 1066, Southampton became the major port of transit between the then capital of England, Winchester, and Normandy. Southampton Castle was built in the 12th century and by the 13th century Southampton had become a leading port, particularly involved in the import of French wine in exchange for English cloth and wool.
rewrite: After the Norman Conquest of 1066, Southampton emerged as the principal port connecting Winchester, then England's capital, to Normandy. The 12th-century construction of Southampton Castle preceded the town's rise to a premier port by the 13th century, heavily engaged in trading English cloth and wool for French wine.

input: Air defence in naval tactics, especially within a carrier group, is often built around a system of concentric layers with the aircraft carrier at the centre. The outer layer will usually be provided by the carrier's aircraft, specifically its AEW&C aircraft combined with the CAP. If an attacker is able to penetrate this layer, then the next layers would come from the surface-to-air missiles carried by the carrier's escorts; the area-defence missiles, such as the RIM-67 Standard, with a range of up to 100 nmi, and the point-defence missiles, like the RIM-162 ESSM, with a range of up to 30 nmi. Finally, virtually every modern warship will be fitted with small-calibre guns, including a CIWS, which is usually a radar-controlled Gatling gun of between 20mm and 30mm calibre capable of firing several thousand rounds per minute.
rewrite: In naval tactics, air defense for a carrier group is typically structured as a series of concentric layers centered on the aircraft carrier. The outermost layer is generally maintained by the carrier's aircraft, specifically its AEW&C planes working in conjunction with the Combat Air Patrol (CAP). Should an attacker breach this layer, the next line of defense comes from surface-to-air missiles launched by the carrier's escort ships. These include area-defense missiles, like the RIM-67 Standard with a range up to 100 nautical miles, and point-defense missiles, such as the RIM-162 ESSM with a range up to 30 nautical miles. Finally, nearly all modern warships are equipped with small-caliber guns, including a Close-In Weapon System (CIWS). This is typically a radar-guided Gatling gun of 20mm to 30mm caliber, capable of firing thousands of rounds per minute.

input: Throughout history there have been a series of lingua francas in the area to allow for better communication. The dialects spoken in Hangzhou, Shaoxing, and Ningbo have taken on this role historically. Since the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, Mandarin, which is not mutually intelligible with any of the local dialects, has been promoted as the standard language of communication throughout China. As a result, most of the population now can, to some degree, speak and comprehend Mandarin and can code-switch when necessary. A majority of the population educated since 1978 can speak Mandarin. Urban residents tend to be more fluent in Mandarin than rural people. Nevertheless, a Zhejiang accent is detectable in almost everyone from the area communicating in Mandarin, and the home dialect remains an important part of the everyday lives and cultural identities of most Zhejiang residents.
rewrite: Historically, a series of lingua francas have emerged in the region to facilitate communication. The dialects of Hangzhou, Shaoxing, and Ningbo have each served this role in the past. Following the establishment of the People's Republic of China in 1949, Mandarin—which is not mutually intelligible with the local dialects—was promoted nationwide as the standard language. Consequently, most of the population can now speak and understand Mandarin to some extent and can code-switch as needed. A majority of those educated since 1978 can speak Mandarin, with urban residents generally demonstrating greater fluency than those in rural areas. Despite this widespread adoption, a Zhejiang accent is almost universally detectable when locals speak Mandarin, and the native dialect continues to be a vital part of daily life and cultural identity for most residents of Zhejiang.

input: The major opponent of Freemasonry was the Roman Catholic Church, so that in countries with a large Catholic element, such as France, Italy, Spain, and Mexico, much of the ferocity of the political battles involve the confrontation between what Davies calls the reactionary Church and enlightened Freemasonry. Even in France, Masons did not act as a group. American historians, while noting that Benjamin Franklin and George Washington were indeed active Masons, have downplayed the importance of Freemasonry in causing the American Revolution because the Masonic order was non-political and included both Patriots and their enemy the Loyalists.
rewrite: The Roman Catholic Church stood as the primary opponent of Freemasonry. Consequently, in nations with significant Catholic populations—like France, Italy, Spain, and Mexico—the fierceness of political strife often stemmed from the clash between what Davies terms the reactionary Church and enlightened Freemasonry. Even in France, Masons did not operate as a unified bloc. Meanwhile, American historians acknowledge Benjamin Franklin and George Washington were active Masons but have minimized Freemasonry's role in causing the American Revolution, noting the order was non-political and included both Patriots and their Loyalist enemies.

input: A German ethnicity emerged in the course of the Middle Ages, ultimately as a result of the formation of the kingdom of Germany within East Francia and later the Holy Roman Empire, beginning in the 9th century. The process was gradual and lacked any clear definition, and the use of exonyms designating "the Germans" develops only during the High Middle Ages. The title of rex teutonicum "King of the Germans" is first used in the late 11th century, by the chancery of Pope Gregory VII, to describe the future Holy Roman Emperor of the German Nation Henry IV. Natively, the term ein diutscher ("a German") is used for the people of Germany from the 12th century.
rewrite: A German ethnicity gradually emerged during the Middle Ages, stemming from the establishment of the German kingdom within East Francia and, later, the Holy Roman Empire from the 9th century onward. This process was slow and undefined, with exonyms for "the Germans" only arising in the High Middle Ages. The title *rex teutonicum*, or "King of the Germans," was first employed in the late 11th century by Pope Gregory VII’s chancery to refer to the future Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV. Natively, the phrase *ein diutscher* ("a German") came into use for the people of Germany from the 12th century.

input: The rise of port cities saw the clustering of populations caused by the development of steamships and railroads. Urbanization increased from 1700 to 1922, with towns and cities growing. Improvements in health and sanitation made them more attractive to live and work in. Port cities like Salonica, in Greece, saw its population rise from 55,000 in 1800 to 160,000 in 1912 and İzmir which had a population of 150,000 in 1800 grew to 300,000 by 1914. Some regions conversely had population falls – Belgrade saw its population drop from 25,000 to 8,000 mainly due to political strife.
rewrite: The rise of steamships and railroads led to population clustering in port cities. From 1700 to 1922, urbanization increased as towns and cities grew, made more attractive by improvements in health and sanitation. For example, Salonica, Greece, saw its population rise from 55,000 in 1800 to 160,000 in 1912, while İzmir grew from 150,000 to 300,000 between 1800 and 1914. Conversely, some regions experienced population declines, such as Belgrade, where numbers fell from 25,000 to 8,000 largely due to political strife.

input: The state is well known for its handicrafts. The carpets, leather works, shawls, metalware, woodwork and paintings are worth appreciating. Pashmina shawls are a product that is highly in demand in Himachal and all over the country. Himachali caps are famous art work of the people. Extreme cold winters of Himachal necessitated wool weaving. Nearly every household in Himachal owns a pit-loom. Wool is considered as pure and is used as a ritual cloth. The well-known woven object is the shawl, ranging from fine pashmina to the coarse desar. Kullu is famous for its shawls with striking patterns and vibrant colours. Kangra and Dharamshala are famous for Kangra miniature paintings.

input: On 16 June 2006, it was announced that Everton had entered into talks with Knowsley Council and Tesco over the possibility of building a new 55,000 seat stadium, expandable to over 60,000, in Kirkby. The club took the unusual move of giving its supporters a say in the club's future by holding a ballot on the proposal, finding a split of 59% to 41% in favour. Opponents to the plan included other local councils concerned by the effect of a large Tesco store being built as part of the development, and a group of fans demanding that Everton should remain within the city boundaries of Liverpool.
rewrite: On 16 June 2006, Everton announced it had entered talks with Knowsley Council and Tesco regarding a potential new stadium in Kirkby. The proposed venue would seat 55,000, with possible expansion to over 60,000. In an unusual move, the club held a ballot for supporters on the proposal, resulting in a 59% to 41% vote in favour. Opponents included other local councils, concerned about the impact of a large Tesco store within the development, and a group of fans insisting Everton must remain within Liverpool's city boundaries.

input: On 25 May 2011 the Swiss government announced that it plans to end its use of nuclear energy in the next 2 or 3 decades. "The government has voted for a phaseout because we want to ensure a secure and autonomous supply of energy", Energy Minister Doris Leuthard said that day at a press conference in Bern. "Fukushima showed that the risk of nuclear power is too high, which in turn has also increased the costs of this energy form." The first reactor would reportedly be taken offline in 2019 and the last one in 2034. Parliament will discuss the plan in June 2011, and there could be a referendum as well.
rewrite: On 25 May 2011, the Swiss government announced a plan to phase out nuclear energy over the next two to three decades. Energy Minister Doris Leuthard stated at a press conference in Bern that the government voted for the phaseout to ensure a secure and autonomous energy supply. She added that the Fukushima disaster demonstrated nuclear power's excessive risks, which have also increased its costs. The first reactor is reportedly scheduled to go offline in 2019, with the last one following in 2034. Parliament will discuss the plan in June 2011, and a referendum could also be held.

input: At the funeral of the tenor Adolphe Nourrit in Paris in 1839, Chopin made a rare appearance at the organ, playing a transcription of Franz Schubert's lied Die Gestirne. On 26 July 1840 Chopin and Sand were present at the dress rehearsal of Berlioz's Grande symphonie funèbre et triomphale, composed to commemorate the tenth anniversary of the July Revolution. Chopin was reportedly unimpressed with the composition.
rewrite: At the 1839 Paris funeral of tenor Adolphe Nourrit, Chopin made a rare organ appearance, performing a transcription of Schubert's lied *Die Gestirne*. Later, on 26 July 1840, Chopin and Sand attended the dress rehearsal for Berlioz's *Grande symphonie funèbre et triomphale*, composed for the July Revolution's tenth anniversary. Chopin was reportedly unimpressed with the work.

input: Nigeria has a varied landscape. The far south is defined by its tropical rainforest climate, where annual rainfall is 60 to 80 inches (1,500 to 2,000 mm) a year. In the southeast stands the Obudu Plateau. Coastal plains are found in both the southwest and the southeast. This forest zone's most southerly portion is defined as "salt water swamp," also known as a mangrove swamp because of the large amount of mangroves in the area. North of this is fresh water swamp, containing different vegetation from the salt water swamp, and north of that is rain forest.
rewrite: Nigeria features a varied landscape. The far south has a tropical rainforest climate, with annual rainfall between 60 and 80 inches (1,500 to 2,000 mm). The Obudu Plateau rises in the southeast, while coastal plains are located in both the southwest and southeast. The most southerly part of this forest zone is the "salt water swamp," or mangrove swamp, characterized by its many mangroves. North of this lies the fresh water swamp, which has different vegetation, and farther north is the rain forest.

input: At the decision-making point of their lives, youth is susceptible to drug addiction, sexual abuse, peer pressure, violent crimes and other illegal activities. input: The most impressive and famous of Sumerian buildings are the ziggurats, large layered platforms which supported temples. Sumerian cylinder seals also depict houses built from reeds not unlike those built by the Marsh Arabs of Southern Iraq until as recently as 400 CE. The Sumerians also developed the arch, which enabled them to develop a strong type of dome. They built this by constructing and linking several arches. Sumerian temples and palaces made use of more advanced materials and techniques,[citation needed] such as buttresses, recesses, half columns, and clay nails.
rewrite: The most impressive and famous Sumerian buildings are the ziggurats, which were large layered platforms supporting temples. Sumerian cylinder seals also show houses built from reeds, similar to those constructed by the Marsh Arabs of Southern Iraq until around 400 CE. Additionally, the Sumerians developed the arch, enabling them to create a strong type of dome by constructing and linking several arches. Their temples and palaces utilized more advanced materials and techniques, such as buttresses, recesses, half columns, and clay nails.

input: After Germany entered a Tripartite Pact with Japan and Italy, Ribbentrop wrote to Stalin, inviting Molotov to Berlin for negotiations aimed to create a 'continental bloc' of Germany, Italy, Japan and the USSR that would oppose Britain and the USA. Stalin sent Molotov to Berlin to negotiate the terms for the Soviet Union to join the Axis and potentially enjoy the spoils of the pact. After negotiations during November 1940 on where to extend the USSR's sphere of influence, Hitler broke off talks and continued planning for the eventual attempts to invade the Soviet Union.
rewrite: After Germany joined the Tripartite Pact with Japan and Italy, Ribbentrop wrote to Stalin, inviting Molotov to Berlin. The goal was to negotiate a ‘continental bloc’ of Germany, Italy, Japan, and the USSR to oppose Britain and the USA. Stalin dispatched Molotov to discuss the Soviet Union joining the Axis and sharing in its potential gains. Following negotiations in November 1940 over expanding the USSR’s sphere of influence, Hitler ended the talks and proceeded with plans to eventually invade the Soviet Union.

input: The Executive Office also supports the U.S. military by providing it with information it gathers, receiving information from military intelligence organizations, and cooperating on field activities. The Executive Director is in charge of the day to day operation of the CIA, and each branch of the service has its own Director. The Associate Director of military affairs, a senior military officer, manages the relationship between the CIA and the Unified Combatant Commands, who produce regional/operational intelligence and consume national intelligence.
rewrite: The Executive Office supports the U.S. military by sharing gathered information, receiving intelligence from military organizations, and cooperating on field activities. The Executive Director oversees the CIA's daily operations, and each service branch has its own Director. A senior military officer serving as the Associate Director of military affairs manages the relationship between the CIA and the Unified Combatant Commands, which produce regional and operational intelligence while utilizing national intelligence.

input: The World Bank reported in February 2009 that the Arab World was far less severely affected by the credit crunch. With generally good balance of payments positions coming into the crisis or with alternative sources of financing for their large current account deficits, such as remittances, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) or foreign aid, Arab countries were able to avoid going to the market in the latter part of 2008. This group is in the best position to absorb the economic shocks. They entered the crisis in exceptionally strong positions. This gives them a significant cushion against the global downturn. The greatest impact of the global economic crisis will come in the form of lower oil prices, which remains the single most important determinant of economic performance. Steadily declining oil prices would force them to draw down reserves and cut down on investments. Significantly lower oil prices could cause a reversal of economic performance as has been the case in past oil shocks. Initial impact will be seen on public finances and employment for foreign workers.
rewrite:
In February 2009, the World Bank reported that the Arab World was far less severely impacted by the credit crunch. Arab countries entered the crisis from exceptionally strong positions, generally with sound balance of payments or with alternative financing sources—such as remittances, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), or foreign aid—to cover their large current account deficits. This allowed them to avoid turning to the market in the latter part of 2008. Consequently, this group is in the best position to absorb economic shocks, possessing a significant cushion against the global downturn.

The greatest impact of the global economic crisis, however, is expected to come from lower oil prices, which remain the single most important determinant of regional economic performance. Steadily declining oil prices would force draw-downs on reserves and reductions in investment. Significantly lower prices could cause a reversal of economic performance, as witnessed in past oil shocks. The initial effects would likely be seen in public finances and in employment for foreign workers.

input: Various music journalists, critical theorists, and authors have deemed Madonna the most influential female recording artist of all time. Author Carol Clerk wrote that "during her career, Madonna has transcended the term 'pop star' to become a global cultural icon." Rolling Stone of Spain wrote that "She became the first viral Master of Pop in history, years before the Internet was massively used. Madonna was everywhere; in the almighty music television channels, 'radio formulas', magazine covers and even in bookshops. A pop dialectic, never seen since The Beatles's reign, which allowed her to keep on the edge of tendency and commerciality." Laura Barcella in her book Madonna and Me: Women Writers on the Queen of Pop (2012) wrote that "really, Madonna changed everything the musical landscape, the '80s look du jour, and most significantly, what a mainstream female pop star could (and couldn't) say, do, or accomplish in the public eye." William Langley from The Daily Telegraph felt that "Madonna has changed the world's social history, has done more things as more different people than anyone else is ever likely to." Alan McGee from The Guardian felt that Madonna is a post-modern art, the likes of which we will never see again. He further asserted that Madonna and Michael Jackson invented the terms Queen and King of Pop.
rewrite: Music journalists, critical theorists, and authors have frequently identified Madonna as the most influential female recording artist in history. Author Carol Clerk observed that Madonna has "transcended the term 'pop star' to become a global cultural icon." Similarly, Rolling Stone of Spain noted, "She became the first viral Master of Pop in history, years before the Internet was massively used. input: Operating at normal power line frequencies, universal motors are often found in a range less than 1000 watts. Universal motors also formed the basis of the traditional railway traction motor in electric railways. In this application, the use of AC to power a motor originally designed to run on DC would lead to efficiency losses due to eddy current heating of their magnetic components, particularly the motor field pole-pieces that, for DC, would have used solid (un-laminated) iron and they are now rarely used.
rewrite: Operating at standard power line frequencies, universal motors are commonly rated under 1000 watts. They also served as the foundation for traditional railway traction motors in electric railways. In such applications, powering a motor originally designed for DC with AC causes efficiency losses from eddy current heating in magnetic components. This especially affected the motor field pole-pieces, which for DC were typically solid iron. Consequently, these motors are now seldom used.

input: Capacitors made with any type of dielectric material will show some level of "dielectric absorption" or "soakage". On discharging a capacitor and disconnecting it, after a short time it may develop a voltage due to hysteresis in the dielectric. This effect can be objectionable in applications such as precision sample and hold circuits or timing circuits. The level of absorption depends on many factors, from design considerations to charging time, since the absorption is a time-dependent process. However, the primary factor is the type of dielectric material. Capacitors such as tantalum electrolytic or polysulfone film exhibit very high absorption, while polystyrene or Teflon allow very small levels of absorption. In some capacitors where dangerous voltages and energies exist, such as in flashtubes, television sets, and defibrillators, the dielectric absorption can recharge the capacitor to hazardous voltages after it has been shorted or discharged. Any capacitor containing over 10 joules of energy is generally considered hazardous, while 50 joules or higher is potentially lethal. A capacitor may regain anywhere from 0.01 to 20% of its original charge over a period of several minutes, allowing a seemingly safe capacitor to become surprisingly dangerous.
rewrite: Capacitors constructed with any dielectric material exhibit a degree of "dielectric absorption" or "soakage." If a capacitor is discharged and then disconnected, it can develop a residual voltage after a short time due to dielectric hysteresis. This effect is particularly problematic in precision applications like sample-and-hold circuits or timing circuits. The extent of absorption depends on several factors, including design and charging time, as it is a time-dependent process. Nevertheless, the primary determinant is the dielectric material itself. Capacitors using tantalum electrolytic or polysulfone film dielectrics show very high absorption, whereas those made with polystyrene or Teflon exhibit minimal levels. In capacitors storing dangerous voltages and energies—such as in flashtubes, television sets, and defibrillators—dielectric absorption can recharge the capacitor to hazardous levels even after it has been shorted or discharged. Any capacitor storing over 10 joules of energy is typically considered hazardous, with 50 joules or more being potentially lethal. A capacitor may recover between 0.01% and 20% of its original charge over several minutes, transforming a seemingly safe component into a surprisingly dangerous one.

input: Rajasthan is famous for its forts, carved temples, and decorated havelis, which were built by Rajput kings in pre-Muslim era Rajasthan.[citation needed] Rajasthan's Jaipur Jantar Mantar, Mehrangarh Fort and Stepwell of Jodhpur, Dilwara Temples, Chittorgarh Fort, Lake Palace, miniature paintings in Bundi, and numerous city palaces and haveli's are part of the architectural heritage of India. Jaipur, the Pink City, is noted for the ancient houses made of a type of sandstone dominated by a pink hue. In Jodhpur, maximum houses are painted blue. At Ajmer, there is white marble Bara-dari on the Anasagar lake. Jain Temples dot Rajasthan from north to south and east to west. Dilwara Temples of Mount Abu, Ranakpur Temple dedicated to Lord Adinath in Pali District, Jain temples in the fort complexes of Chittor, Jaisalmer and Kumbhalgarh, Lodurva Jain temples, Mirpur Jain Temple, Sarun Mata Temple kotputli, Bhandasar and Karni Mata Temple of Bikaner and Mandore of Jodhpur are some of the best examples.
rewrite: Rajasthan is renowned for its forts, carved temples, and decorated havelis, many constructed by Rajput kings in the pre-Muslim era. Notable architectural heritage sites include Jaipur's Jantar Mantar, Mehrangarh Fort and the Stepwell in Jodhpur, the Dilwara Temples, Chittorgarh Fort, the Lake Palace, Bundi's miniature paintings, and numerous city palaces and havelis. Jaipur, the Pink City, is distinguished by ancient houses built from a type of sandstone with a dominant pink hue. In Jodhpur, most houses are painted blue. Ajmer features a white marble Bara-dari on Anasagar Lake. Jain temples are found throughout Rajasthan. Prime examples include the Dilwara Temples of Mount Abu, the Ranakpur Temple dedicated to Lord Adinath in Pali District, Jain temples within the fort complexes of Chittor, Jaisalmer and Kumbhalgarh, the Lodurva Jain temples, Mirpur Jain Temple, Sarun Mata Temple in Kotputli, and the Bhandasar and Karni Mata Temples of Bikaner, along with Mandore in Jodhpur.

input: The primary circadian "clock" in mammals is located in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (or nuclei) (SCN), a pair of distinct groups of cells located in the hypothalamus. Destruction of the SCN results in the complete absence of a regular sleep–wake rhythm. The SCN receives information about illumination through the eyes. The retina of the eye contains "classical" photoreceptors ("rods" and "cones"), which are used for conventional vision. But the retina also contains specialized ganglion cells that are directly photosensitive, and project directly to the SCN, where they help in the entrainment (synchronization) of this master circadian clock.
rewrite: In mammals, the main circadian "clock" resides in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a distinct pair of cell groups within the hypothalamus. Destroying the SCN completely eliminates regular sleep–wake rhythms. This master clock receives light information through the eyes. The retina contains "classical" photoreceptors—rods and cones—for standard vision. Additionally, it holds specialized, directly photosensitive ganglion cells that project straight to the SCN, aiding in the entrainment, or synchronization, of this central circadian clock.

input: In a response to Livingstone, Theodore Dobzhansky argued that when talking about race one must be attentive to how the term is being used: "I agree with Dr. Livingstone that if races have to be 'discrete units,' then there are no races, and if 'race' is used as an 'explanation' of the human variability, rather than vice versa, then the explanation is invalid." He further argued that one could use the term race if one distinguished between "race differences" and "the race concept." The former refers to any distinction in gene frequencies between populations; the latter is "a matter of judgment." He further observed that even when there is clinal variation, "Race differences are objectively ascertainable biological phenomena… but it does not follow that racially distinct populations must be given racial (or subspecific) labels." In short, Livingstone and Dobzhansky agree that there are genetic differences among human beings; they also agree that the use of the race concept to classify people, and how the race concept is used, is a matter of social convention. They differ on whether the race concept remains a meaningful and useful social convention.
rewrite: In response to Livingstone, Theodore Dobzhansky argued that one must be attentive to how the term "race" is being used. He stated: "I agree with Dr. Livingstone that if races have to be 'discrete units,' then there are no races, and if 'race' is used as an 'explanation' of human variability, rather than vice versa, then the explanation is invalid." Dobzhansky further contended that the term could be used if one distinguished between "race differences" and "the race concept." He defined "race differences" as any distinction in gene frequencies between populations, while calling the race concept itself "a matter of judgment." He also observed that even with clinal variation, "Race differences are objectively ascertainable biological phenomena… but it does not follow that racially distinct populations must be given racial (or subspecific) labels." In summary, Livingstone and Dobzhansky agree on the existence of genetic differences among humans and that applying the race concept to classify people is a social convention. Their disagreement lies in whether the race concept remains a meaningful and useful social convention.

input: As the Kulluk oil rig was being towed to the American state of Washington to be serviced in preparation for the 2013 drilling season, a winter storm on 27 December 2012 caused the towing crews, as well as the rescue service, to lose control of the situation. As of 1 January 2013, the Kulluk was grounded off the coast Sitkalidak Island, near the eastern end of Kodiak Island. Following the accident, a Fortune magazine contacted Larry McKinney, the executive director at the Harte Research Institute for Gulf of Mexico Studies at Texas A&M, and he explained that "A two-month delay in the Arctic is not a two-month delay ... A two-month delay could wipe out the entire drilling season."
rewrite: While being towed to Washington state for servicing ahead of the 2013 drilling season, the Kulluk oil rig encountered a winter storm on December 27, 2012. The storm caused the towing and rescue crews to lose control. By January 1, 2013, the rig had grounded off the coast of Sitkalidak Island, near the eastern end of Kodiak Island. After the accident, a Fortune magazine contacted Larry McKinney, executive director of the Harte Research Institute for Gulf of Mexico Studies at Texas A&M. He explained that in the Arctic, "A two-month delay is not a two-month delay ... A two-month delay could wipe out the entire drilling season."

input: In the later 1890s and into first decade of the 20th century, structural changes occurred in the operation of the Pacific trading companies; they moved from a practice of having traders resident on each island to instead becoming a business operation where the supercargo (the cargo manager of a trading ship) would deal directly with the islanders when a ship visited an island. From 1900 the numbers of palagi traders in Tuvalu declined and the last of the palagi traders were Fred Whibley on Niutao, Alfred Restieaux on Nukufetau, and Martin Kleis on Nui. By 1909 there were no more resident palagi traders representing the trading companies, although both Whibley and Restieaux remained in the islands until their deaths.
rewrite: In the late 1890s and early 1900s, the operations of Pacific trading companies underwent structural changes. They shifted from maintaining resident traders on each island to a system where the supercargo—the cargo manager of a trading ship—would conduct business directly with islanders during a ship's visit. From 1900, the number of palagi traders in Tuvalu declined. The last of these traders were Fred Whibley on Niutao, Alfred Restieaux on Nukufetau, and Martin Kleis on Nui. By 1909, no resident palagi traders represented the companies, though Whibley and Restieaux remained in the islands until their deaths.

input: Mu'awiyah introduced postal service, Abd al-Malik extended it throughout his empire, and Walid made full use of it. The Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik developed a regular postal service. Umar bin Abdul-Aziz developed it further by building caravanserais at stages along the Khurasan highway. Relays of horses were used for the conveyance of dispatches between the caliph and his agents and officials posted in the provinces. The main highways were divided into stages of 12 miles (19 km) each and each stage had horses, donkeys or camels ready to carry the post. Primarily the service met the needs of Government officials, but travellers and their important dispatches were also benefitted by the system. The postal carriages were also used for the swift transport of troops. They were able to carry fifty to a hundred men at a time. Under Governor Yusuf bin Umar, the postal department of Iraq cost 4,000,000 dirhams a year.
rewrite: Mu'awiyah introduced the postal service, which Abd al-Malik then extended throughout his empire and Walid fully utilized. Caliph Abd al-Malik developed this into a regular service. Umar bin Abdul-Aziz furthered its development by constructing caravanserais at stages along the Khurasan highway. Relays of horses conveyed dispatches between the caliph and his provincial agents and officials. The main highways were divided into stages of 12 miles (19 km) each, with horses, donkeys, or camels ready at every stage to carry the post. While the service primarily met the needs of government officials, travellers and their important dispatches also benefited from the system. The postal carriages were additionally used for the swift transport of troops, carrying fifty to a hundred men at a time. Under Governor Yusuf bin Umar, the postal department of Iraq cost 4,000,000 dirhams a year.

input: Ziggurats (Sumerian temples) each had an individual name and consisted of a forecourt, with a central pond for purification. The temple itself had a central nave with aisles along either side. Flanking the aisles would be rooms for the priests. At one end would stand the podium and a mudbrick table for animal and vegetable sacrifices. Granaries and storehouses were usually located near the temples. After a time the Sumerians began to place the temples on top of multi-layered square constructions built as a series of rising terraces, giving rise to the Ziggurat style.
rewrite: Each ziggurat, a Sumerian temple, possessed its own name and featured a forecourt with a central purification pond. The temple building contained a central nave flanked by aisles, alongside which were rooms for the priests. At one end stood a podium and a mudbrick table for animal and vegetable sacrifices. Granaries and storehouses were typically situated near the temples. Over time, the Sumerians began constructing these temples atop multi-layered square bases, built as a series of rising terraces, which led to the distinctive Ziggurat style.

input: Additionally, there are issues of connections between different electrical services, particularly connecting intercity lines with sections electrified for commuter traffic, but also between commuter lines built to different standards. This can cause electrification of certain connections to be very expensive simply because of the implications on the sections it is connecting. Many lines have come to be overlaid with multiple electrification standards for different trains to avoid having to replace the existing rolling stock on those lines. Obviously, this requires that the economics of a particular connection must be more compelling and this has prevented complete electrification of many lines. In a few cases, there are diesel trains running along completely electrified routes and this can be due to incompatibility of electrification standards along the route.
rewrite: Furthermore, challenges arise in linking various electrical systems, especially when connecting intercity lines with segments electrified for commuter traffic, as well as between commuter lines constructed under differing standards. This can make electrifying certain connections prohibitively costly due to the impacts on the sections being joined. To avoid replacing existing rolling stock, many lines have accumulated multiple electrification standards to accommodate different trains. Consequently, the economics of any given connection must be especially favorable, which has hindered the full electrification of numerous lines. In some instances, diesel trains operate on entirely electrified routes because of incompatible electrification standards along the way.

input: Yale's Office of Sustainability develops and implements sustainability practices at Yale. Yale is committed to reduce its greenhouse gas emissions 10% below 1990 levels by the year 2020. As part of this commitment, the university allocates renewable energy credits to offset some of the energy used by residential colleges. Eleven campus buildings are candidates for LEED design and certification. Yale Sustainable Food Project initiated the introduction of local, organic vegetables, fruits, and beef to all residential college dining halls. Yale was listed as a Campus Sustainability Leader on the Sustainable Endowments Institute’s College Sustainability Report Card 2008, and received a "B+" grade overall.
rewrite: Yale's Office of Sustainability is responsible for developing and implementing the university's sustainability practices. Yale is committed to reducing its greenhouse gas emissions to 10% below 1990 levels by 2020. To support this goal, the university uses renewable energy credits to offset a portion of the energy consumed by its residential colleges. Eleven campus buildings are candidates for LEED design and certification. Furthermore, the Yale Sustainable Food Project has introduced local, organic vegetables, fruits, and beef into all residential college dining halls. Yale was recognized as a Campus Sustainability Leader and received an overall grade of "B+" on the Sustainable Endowments Institute’s College Sustainability Report Card 2008.

input: Paul VI was the first pope to receive an Anglican Archbishop of Canterbury, Michael Ramsey in official audience as Head of Church, after the private audience visit of Archbishop Geoffrey Fisher to Pope John XXIII on 2 December 1960. Ramsey met Paul three times during his visit and opened the Anglican Centre in Rome to increase their mutual knowledge. He praised Paul VI[e] and his contributions in the service of unity. Paul replied that "by entering into our house, you are entering your own house, we are happy to open our door and heart to you." The two Church leaders signed a common declaration, which put an end to the disputes of the past and outlined a common agenda for the future.
rewrite: Paul VI became the first pope to officially receive an Anglican Archbishop of Canterbury, Michael Ramsey, as Head of the Church. This followed a private audience between Archbishop Geoffrey Fisher and Pope John XXIII on 2 December 1960. During his visit, Ramsey met with Paul VI on three occasions and inaugurated the Anglican Centre in Rome to foster mutual understanding. Ramsey praised Paul VI and his work toward Christian unity. In response, Paul VI stated, "by entering into our house, you are entering your own house, we are happy to open our door and heart to you." Together, the two leaders signed a common declaration. This document ended past disputes and established a shared agenda for the future.

input: Pippy Park is an urban park located in the east end of the city; with over 3,400 acres (14 km2) of land, it is one of Canada's largest urban parks. The park contains a range of recreational facilities including two golf courses, Newfoundland and Labrador's largest serviced campground, walking and skiing trails as well as protected habitat for many plants and animals. Pippy Park is also home to the Fluvarium, an environmental education centre which offers a cross section view of Nagle's Hill Brook.
rewrite: Pippy Park is a large urban park situated in the city's east end. Encompassing over 3,400 acres (14 km2), it ranks among Canada's largest urban parks. Its recreational facilities include two golf courses, the largest serviced campground in Newfoundland and Labrador, and trails for walking and skiing, alongside protected habitats for numerous plants and animals. The park also houses the Fluvarium, an environmental education centre featuring a cross-section view of Nagle's Hill Brook.

input: Hyderabad is the largest contributor to the gross domestic product (GDP), tax and other revenues, of Telangana, and the sixth largest deposit centre and fourth largest credit centre nationwide, as ranked by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in June 2012. Its US$74 billion GDP made it the fifth-largest contributor city to India's overall GDP in 2011–12. Its per capita annual income in 2011 was ₹44300 (US$660). As of 2006[update], the largest employers in the city were the governments of Andhra Pradesh (113,098 employees) and India (85,155). According to a 2005 survey, 77% of males and 19% of females in the city were employed. The service industry remains dominant in the city, and 90% of the employed workforce is engaged in this sector.
rewrite: Hyderabad is the largest contributor to the gross domestic product (GDP) and to tax and other revenues for Telangana. Nationally, it is ranked by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as the sixth largest deposit centre and the fourth largest credit centre, based on a June 2012 assessment. In the 2011–12 period, the city's US$74 billion GDP made it India's fifth-largest urban contributor to the national GDP. Its per capita annual income in 2011 was ₹44,300 (US$660).
